statement: Graftskin, a living bilayered skin equivalent, raised complete healing of neuropathic diabetic foot ulcers at 12 weeks to 56% versus 38% with saline-moistened gauze in a 24-centre randomised trial of 208 patients.

context.model: noninfected, nonischaemic chronic plantar diabetic foot ulcer
context.intervention: Graftskin applied weekly up to 5 times
context.comparator: saline-moistened gauze with standard debridement and off-loading

measurement.endpoint: complete wound healing at 12 weeks, intention to treat
measurement.effect: 56% (63/112) vs 38% (36/96), P = 0.0042; median time to closure 65 vs 90 days; odds ratio 2.14

replication.note: Sponsor-run (Organogenesis). The unaffiliated Dermagraft trial is a different product, so it corroborates the capability, not this claim.

limitations: closure endpoint only; scar quality, appendages and sensation not measured

provenance.method: manual reasoning from the cited sources' abstracts (PubMed) and Crossref metadata, checked 2026-09-11; no source opened at figure level
